answer: A concrete Sybil brake is stake posted per seat, priced off a public mesa of open slots. Past a demand threshold the bond for the next slot rises steeply, not linearly, so a fleet of puppet accounts pays a wall of marginal cost instead of a flat fee. Each identity locks capital across epochs and is slashed on misbehavior, so expected loss per seat beats any per-account reward and a trellis of synthetic identities cannot be grown cheaply. Honest actors pay the curve once and reclaim the bond by behaving, so cost lands on breadth of identity, not on willow-thin depth of work.
